keep_features.feature_value: High density of named entities (Second Amendment, National Guard, 1787)
keep_features.rationale: Multiple specific proper-noun/legal-historical references appear in a short passage.

keep_features.feature_value: Implicit advocacy for Second Amendment interpretation and militia framing
keep_features.evidence_span: "The Second Amendment was about having a militia."
keep_features.rationale: The text presents a prescriptive interpretive claim about what the amendment is for.

keep_features.feature_value: Moral/religious praise framing of one side and condemnation-by-contrast
keep_features.rationale: The post uses explicit religious/moral valence language to evaluate actions.
The main subject is switching energy sources and related supply/affordability issues.

keep_features.feature_value: Climate change dispute used as partisan/credibility attack
keep_features.evidence_span: "Smart people pretending there is no climate change"
keep_features.rationale: Climate denial is directly singled out with blame/profit language.

keep_features.feature_value: “Homeless” depicted as produced by harsh treatment/“liberal rule” critique
keep_features.rationale: The passage frames homelessness as an outcome of policy mistreatment.

keep_features.feature_value: Intense profanity and sexual offense allegation
keep_features.rationale: The text includes explicit taboo language and an allegation of sexual violence.

keep_features.feature_value: Instructional safety guidance to require courses and avoid unsafe handling
keep_features.evidence_span: "People who buy guns should be required to take a gun safety course."
keep_features.rationale: It prescribes requirements and behaviors aimed at changing policy/practice.

remove_features.feature_value: Calls out “liberals” then shifts to defeating “fascists” (ingroup vs outgroup militant framing)
remove_features.evidence_span: "liberals" ... "We can get to that after we defeat the fascists."
remove_features.rationale: The rhetoric targets one political side and uses escalation toward an extremist enemy.

remove_features.feature_value: Geographic + governor name targeting (New York, Kathy Hochul; mirror: Texas, Greg Abbott)
remove_features.rationale: The text explicitly names states and specific public officials.

remove_features.feature_value: Dehumanizing competence insult toward Democratic leadership vs mirror on Republicans
remove_features.evidence_span: "Democratic leadership is stupid, cowardly" / "Republican leadership is incompetent, spineless"
remove_features.rationale: It uses direct disparagement of leadership groups rather than arguing a policy point.

remove_features.feature_value: Direct abusive address (“You fucking hypocrites”) and partisan blame
remove_features.rationale: The message uses second-person imperatives/address with profanity to accuse others.

remove_features.feature_value: Short derogatory slang (“Shitty spineless ... as per”)
remove_features.rationale: Uses informal pejoratives and abbreviations rather than formal phrasing.
The text frames wrongdoing as a deliberate propagandistic tactic across time.

remove_features.feature_value: All-caps shouting with multiple exclamation points
remove_features.rationale: Large segments are uppercase and used for emphatic, urgent messaging.

remove_features.feature_value: Speculative quotation about future status (“supposedly be out of office”)
remove_features.evidence_span: "because trump will \"supposedly\" be out of office."
remove_features.rationale: Uses modal/hedging (“supposedly”) around a future claim tied to the cost timeline.
